sanskrit: hayānāṃ heṣamāṇānāṃ yodhānāṃ tatra garjatām kṣaṇena khaṃ diśaś caiva śabdenāpūritaṃ tadā
english: From the neighing of the horses and the roaring of the warriors there, in an instant the sky and all the quarters were filled with the din.

sanskrit: putrāṇāṃ tava durdharṣa pāṇḍavānāṃ tathaiva ca samakampanta sainyāni parasparasamāgame
english: O unassailable king, the armies of your sons and of the Pāṇḍavas alike trembled as they came together against one another.

sanskrit: tatra nāgā rathāś caiva jāmbūnadavibhūṣitāḥ bhrājamānā vyadṛśyanta meghā iva savidyutaḥ
english: There the elephants and the chariots, adorned with gold, were seen gleaming like clouds shot through with lightning.

sanskrit: dhvajā bahuvidhākārās tāvakānāṃ narādhipa kāñcanāṅgadino rejur jvalitā iva pāvakāḥ
english: The banners of your men, O lord of men, fashioned in manifold shapes and ringed with golden armlets, shone like blazing fires.

sanskrit: sveṣāṃ caiva pareṣāṃ ca samadṛśyanta bhārata mahendraketavaḥ śubhrā mahendrasadaneṣv iva
english: Among your own and among the foe alike, O Bhārata, the great standards of Indra appeared, gleaming white as in the halls of mighty Indra himself.

sanskrit: kāñcanaiḥ kavacair vīrā jvalanārkasamaprabhaiḥ saṃnaddhāḥ pratyadṛśyanta grahāḥ prajvalitā iva
english: Girt in golden corselets bright as fire and the sun, the heroes appeared like blazing planets.

sanskrit: udyatair āyudhaiś citrais talabaddhāḥ patākinaḥ ṛṣabhākṣā maheṣvāsāś camūmukhagatā babhuḥ
english: With raised and gleaming weapons, leather-guards bound to their hands, bearing pennons, bull-eyed and mighty archers, they shone at the front of the host.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhagopās tu bhīṣmasya putrās tava narādhipa duḥśāsano durviṣaho durmukho duḥsahas tathā
english: As guardians of Bhīṣma's rear, O lord of men, stood your sons—Duḥśāsana, Durviṣaha, Durmukha, and Duḥsaha as well,

sanskrit: viviṃśatiś citraseno vikarṇaś ca mahārathaḥ satyavrataḥ purumitro jayo bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ
english: Viviṃśati, Citrasena, and Vikarṇa the great chariot-warrior, Satyavrata, Purumitra, Jaya, Bhūriśravas, and Śala.

sanskrit: rathā viṃśatisāhasrās tathaiṣām anuyāyinaḥ abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ
english: Twenty thousand chariots followed in their train—the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis,

sanskrit: śālvā matsyās tathāmbaṣṭhās trigartāḥ kekayās tathā sauvīrāḥ kitavāḥ prācyāḥ pratīcyodīcyamālavāḥ
english: the Śālvas, the Matsyas, the Ambaṣṭhas, the Trigartas and the Kekayas, the Sauvīras, the Kitavas, and the men of the East, the West, the North, and the Mālavas.

sanskrit: dvādaśaite janapadāḥ sarve śūrās tanutyajaḥ mahatā rathavaṃśena te 'bhyarakṣan pitāmaham
english: These twelve peoples, all heroes ready to lay down their lives, guarded the grandsire with a great array of chariots.

sanskrit: anīkaṃ daśasāhasraṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām māgadho yena nṛpatis tad rathānīkam anvayāt
english: A division of ten thousand swift elephants, led by the king of Magadha, followed behind that array of chariots.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ cakrarakṣāś ca pādarakṣāś ca dantinām abhūvan vāhinīmadhye śatānām ayutāni ṣaṭ
english: As wheel-guards for the chariots and foot-guards for the tuskers, there were in the midst of the host six myriads of hundreds.

sanskrit: pādātāś cāgrato 'gacchan dhanuścarmāsipāṇayaḥ anekaśatasāhasrā nakharaprāsayodhinaḥ
english: In front marched the foot-soldiers, bearing bows, shields, and swords—many hundreds of thousands, fighting with claw-spears and javelins.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo daśaikā ca tava putrasya bhārata adṛśyanta mahārāja gaṅgeva yamunāntare
english: Eleven akṣauhiṇīs of your son, O Bhārata, were seen, great king, like the Gaṅgā within the bounds of the Yamunā.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca akṣauhiṇyo daśaikāṃ ca vyūḍhāṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ katham alpena sainyena pratyavyūhata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Beholding the eleven akṣauhiṇīs arrayed, how did Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava draw up his counter-array with so small a force?

sanskrit: yo veda mānuṣaṃ vyūhaṃ daivaṃ gāndharvam āsuram kathaṃ bhīṣmaṃ sa kaunteyaḥ pratyavyūhata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: He who knows the human battle-array and the divine, the gandharva and the demonic—how did that son of Kuntī, the Pāṇḍava, array his forces against Bhīṣma?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dhārtarāṣṭrāṇy anīkāni dṛṣṭvā vyūḍhāni pāṇḍavaḥ abhyabhāṣata dharmātmā dharmarājo dhanaṃjayam
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding the divisions of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son drawn up in array, the righteous-souled Pāṇḍava, the king of justice, spoke thus to Dhanaṃjaya:

sanskrit: maharṣer vacanāt tāta vedayanti bṛhaspateḥ saṃhatān yodhayed alpān kāmaṃ vistārayed bahūn
english: By the word of the great seer Bṛhaspati, my dear, they teach this: let a small force fight close-massed, but let a large one spread out at will.

sanskrit: sūcīmukham anīkaṃ syād alpānāṃ bahubhiḥ saha asmākaṃ ca tathā sainyam alpīyaḥ sutarāṃ paraiḥ
english: For the few against the many the array should be needle-pointed; and our army is far smaller than the enemy's.

sanskrit: etad vacanam ājñāya maharṣer vyūha pāṇḍava tac chrutvā dharmarājasya pratyabhāṣata phalguṇaḥ
english: "Heeding this word of the great seer, draw up the array, O Pāṇḍava." Hearing this from the king of justice, Phalguna replied:

sanskrit: eṣa vyūhāmi te rājan vyūhaṃ paramadurjayam acalaṃ nāma vajrākhyaṃ vihitaṃ vajrapāṇinā
english: "This array I shall set in order for you, O king—an array most hard to conquer, the unshakable one called Vajra, ordained by the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa vāta ivoddhūtaḥ samare duḥsahaḥ paraiḥ sa naḥ puro yotsyati vai bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: He who, like a rising wind, is unbearable to the foe in battle—Bhīma, best of strikers—shall fight in our van.

sanskrit: tejāṃsi ripusainyānāṃ mṛdnan puruṣasattamaḥ agre 'graṇīr yāsyati no yuddhopāyavicakṣaṇaḥ
english: Crushing the splendor of the enemy's hosts, that best of men, skilled in the arts of war, shall go before us as our foremost leader.

sanskrit: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthivāḥ sarve duryodhanapurogamāḥ nivartiṣyanti saṃbhrāntāḥ siṃhaṃ kṣudramṛgā iva
english: At the sight of whom all the kings led by Duryodhana will turn back in panic, as small beasts before a lion.

sanskrit: taṃ sarve saṃśrayiṣyāmaḥ prākāram akutobhayam bhīmaṃ praharatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vajrapāṇim ivāmarāḥ
english: Him we shall all take as our fearless rampart—Bhīma, best of strikers—as the immortals take refuge in the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: na hi so 'sti pumāṃl loke yaḥ saṃkruddhaṃ vṛkodaram draṣṭum atyugrakarmāṇaṃ viṣaheta nararṣabham
english: For there is no man in the world who could bear even to look upon Vṛkodara enraged, that bull among men of most terrible deeds.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno gadāṃ bibhrad vajrasāramayīṃ dṛḍhām caran vegena mahatā samudram api śoṣayet
english: Bhīmasena, bearing his firm mace forged with the strength of the thunderbolt, ranging on with mighty speed, could dry up even the ocean."

sanskrit: kekayā dhṛṣṭaketuś ca cekitānaś ca vīryavān eta tiṣṭhanti sāmātyāḥ prekṣakās te nareśvara
english: "The Kekayas, Dhṛṣṭaketu, and the valiant Cekitāna—these stand by with their counselors as your onlookers, O lord of men,

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dāyādā iti bībhatsur abravīt bruvāṇaṃ tu tathā pārthaṃ sarvasainyāni māriṣa apūjayaṃs tadā vāgbhir anukūlābhir āhave
english: as heirs against Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons," said Bībhatsu. And as Pārtha spoke thus, O honored one, all the troops honored him then in the battle with words of approval.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhus tathā cakre dhanaṃjayaḥ vyūhya tāni balāny āśu prayayau phalgunas tadā
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya did so; and having swiftly arrayed those forces, Phalguna then advanced.

sanskrit: saṃprayātān kurūn dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūḥ gaṅgeva pūrṇā stimitā syandamānā vyadṛśyata
english: Beholding the Kurus set in motion, the great host of the Pāṇḍavas appeared like the Gaṅgā in flood—still yet flowing on.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'graṇīs teṣāṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca dhṛṣṭaketuś ca vīryavān
english: Their foremost were Bhīmasena and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, Nakula and Sahadeva, and the valiant Dhṛṣṭaketu.

sanskrit: samudyojya tataḥ paścād rājāpy akṣauhiṇīvṛtaḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha putraiś ca so 'bhyarakṣata pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Then, marshaling them, the king too, encircled by an akṣauhiṇī, together with his brothers and sons, guarded the rear behind.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣau tu bhīmasya mādrīputrau mahādyutī draupadeyāḥ sasaubhadrāḥ pṛṣṭhagopās tarasvinaḥ
english: As wheel-guards of Bhīma stood the two sons of Mādrī of great luster, while the swift sons of Draupadī together with Subhadrā's son guarded his rear.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pāñcālyas teṣāṃ goptā mahārathaḥ sahitaḥ pṛtanāśūrai rathamukhyaiḥ prabhadrakaiḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna of Pāñcāla, that great chariot-warrior, was their protector, joined by the heroes of the host, the foremost charioteers, the Prabhadrakas.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu tataḥ paścād arjunenābhirakṣitaḥ yatto bhīṣmavināśāya prayayau bharatarṣabha
english: Behind him came Śikhaṇḍin, guarded by Arjuna and bent upon the destruction of Bhīṣma, advancing on, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhagopo 'rjunasyāpi yuyudhāno mahārathaḥ cakrarakṣau tu pāñcālyau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau
english: As Arjuna's rear-guard rode Yuyudhāna, the great chariot-warrior, and his wheel-guards were the two Pāñcālas, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas.

sanskrit: rājā tu madhyamānīke kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bṛhadbhiḥ kuñjarair mattaiś caladbhir acalair iva
english: The king Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, stood in the central division, with huge rutting elephants that moved like moving mountains.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyā ca pāñcālyo yajñaseno mahāmanāḥ virāṭam anvayāt paścāt pāṇḍavārthe parākramī
english: And the high-minded Yajñasena of Pāñcāla, with an akṣauhiṇī, valorous in the Pāṇḍavas' cause, followed Virāṭa from behind.

sanskrit: teṣām ādityacandrābhāḥ kanakottamabhūṣaṇāḥ nānācihnadharā rājan ratheṣv āsan mahādhvajāḥ
english: Their great banners, bright as sun and moon, adorned with finest gold and bearing diverse emblems, O king, stood upon the chariots.

sanskrit: samutsarpya tataḥ paścād dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha putraiś ca so 'bhyarakṣad yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then, moving up from behind, Dhṛṣṭadyumna the great chariot-warrior, together with his brothers and sons, guarded Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tvadīyānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca ratheṣu vividhān dhvajān abhibhūyārjunasyaiko dhvajas tasthau mahākapiḥ
english: Surpassing the manifold banners upon the chariots of your men and of the foe, Arjuna's single standard, the great ape, stood high above all.

sanskrit: pādātās tv agrato 'gacchann asiśaktyṛṣṭipāṇayaḥ anekaśatasāhasrā bhīmasenasya rakṣiṇaḥ
english: In front marched the foot-soldiers, bearing swords, spears, and lances—many hundreds of thousands, the protectors of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: vāraṇā daśasāhasrāḥ prabhinnakaraṭāmukhāḥ śūrā hemamayair jālair dīpyamānā ivācalāḥ
english: Ten thousand elephants, their cheeks and faces flowing with rut, gleaming in nets of gold, blazed like mountains.

sanskrit: kṣaranta iva jīmūtā madārdrāḥ padmagandhinaḥ rājānam anvayuḥ paścāc calanta iva parvatāḥ
english: Like raining clouds, wet with rut and fragrant as lotuses, they followed the king from behind like moving mountains.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno gadāṃ bhīmāṃ prakarṣan parighopamām pracakarṣa mahat sainyaṃ durādharṣo mahāmanāḥ
english: Bhīmasena, brandishing his fearsome mace that resembled an iron bar, the high-minded and unassailable one, drew on that mighty host.

sanskrit: tam arkam iva duṣprekṣyaṃ tapantaṃ raśmimālinam na śekuḥ sarvato yodhāḥ prativīkṣitum antike
english: Him, hard to look upon as the burning, ray-wreathed sun, the warriors on every side could not bear to gaze upon at close quarters.

sanskrit: vajro nāmaiṣa tu vyūho durbhidaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ cāpavidyuddhvajo ghoro gupto gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: This was the array named Vajra, hard to break, facing every way—terrible, its banners flashing like lightning over the bow, guarded by the wielder of Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: yaṃ prativyūhya tiṣṭhanti pāṇḍavās tava vāhinīm ajeyo mānuṣe loke pāṇḍavair abhirakṣitaḥ
english: Having arrayed it against your host, the Pāṇḍavas stood firm—an array unconquerable in the world of men, guarded by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: saṃdhyāṃ tiṣṭhatsu sainyeṣu sūryasyodayanaṃ prati prāvāt sapṛṣato vāyur anabhre stanayitnumān
english: As the armies stood at the twilight hour, toward the rising of the sun a wind blew, scattering droplets, thundering though no cloud was there.

sanskrit: viṣvagvātāś ca vānty ugrā nīcaiḥ śarkarakarṣiṇaḥ rajaś coddhūyamānaṃ tu tamasāc chādayaj jagat
english: Fierce winds blew from every side, sweeping up grit low along the ground, and the dust that was raised veiled the world in darkness.

sanskrit: papāta mahatī colkā prāṅmukhī bharatarṣabha udyantaṃ sūryam āhatya vyaśīryata mahāsvanā
english: A great meteor fell, facing eastward, O bull of the Bhāratas, and striking the rising sun, it burst asunder with a mighty roar.

sanskrit: atha sajjīyamāneṣu sainyeṣu bharatarṣabha niṣprabho 'bhyudiyāt sūryaḥ saghoṣo bhūś cacāla ha vyaśīryata sanādā ca tadā bharatasattama
english: Then, as the armies were being made ready, O bull of the Bhāratas, the sun rose dim, and with a great noise the earth shook and split asunder with a roar, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: nirghātā bahavo rājan dikṣu sarvāsu cābhavan prādurāsīd rajas tīvraṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: Many thunderclaps broke out in all the quarters, O king, and a thick dust arose so that nothing at all could be discerned.

sanskrit: dhvajānāṃ dhūyamānānāṃ sahasā mātariśvanā kiṅkiṇījālanaddhānāṃ kāñcanasragvatāṃ ravaiḥ
english: With the sudden tossing by the wind of the banners, hung with networks of little bells and wreathed in gold, and with their jangling,

sanskrit: mahatāṃ sapatākānām ādityasamatejasām sarvaṃ jhaṇajhaṇībhūtam āsīt tālavaneṣv iva
english: those great pennoned standards, splendid as the sun, set everything ringing with their clang, as in groves of fan-palms.

sanskrit: evaṃ te puruṣavyāghrāḥ pāṇḍavā yuddhanandinaḥ vyavasthitāḥ prativyūhya tava putrasya vāhinīm
english: Thus those tigers among men, the Pāṇḍavas, exulting in battle, stood arrayed against your son's host.

sanskrit: sraṃsanta iva majjāno yodhānāṃ bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭvāgrato bhīmasenaṃ gadāpāṇim avasthitam
english: The very marrow of the warriors seemed to melt away, O bull of the Bhāratas, at the sight of Bhīmasena stationed in front, mace in hand.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sūryodaye saṃjaya ke nu pūrvaṃ; yuyutsavo hṛṣyamāṇā ivāsan māmakā vā bhīṣmanetrāḥ samīke; pāṇḍavā vā bhīmanetrās tadānīm
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: At sunrise, Saṃjaya, which were the first, eager to fight and seeming to rejoice—my men led by Bhīṣma upon the field, or the Pāṇḍavas led by Bhīma at that hour?

sanskrit: keṣāṃ jaghanyau somasūryau savāyū; keṣāṃ senāṃ śvāpadā vyābhaṣanta keṣāṃ yūnāṃ mukhavarṇāḥ prasannāḥ; sarvaṃ hy etad brūhi tattvaṃ yathāvat
english: To whose rear were moon, sun, and wind? At whose army did the beasts of prey howl? Whose young men's faces were serene? Tell me all this truly, as it was.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ubhe sene tulyam ivopayāte; ubhe vyūhe hṛṣṭarūpe narendra ubhe citre vanarājiprakāśe; tathaivobhe nāgarathāśvapūrṇe
english: Saṃjaya said: Both armies advanced as if matched, O lord of men; both arrays wore an exultant aspect; both were splendid, gleaming like rows of forest, and both were filled with elephants, chariots, and horses.

sanskrit: ubhe sene bṛhatī bhīmarūpe; tathaivobhe bhārata durviṣahye tathaivobhe svargajayāya sṛṣṭe; tathā hy ubhe satpuruṣāryagupte
english: Both armies were vast and fearsome in form, O Bhārata, and both alike unbearable; both were marshaled for the winning of heaven, and both were guarded by good and noble men.

sanskrit: paścānmukhāḥ kuravo dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ; sthitāḥ pārthāḥ prāṅmukhā yotsyamānāḥ daityendraseneva ca kauravāṇāṃ; devendraseneva ca pāṇḍavānām
english: The Kurus, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, stood facing westward; the Pārthas, ready to fight, faced east. The host of the Kauravas was like the army of the lord of the Daityas, and the host of the Pāṇḍavas like the army of the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: śukro vāyuḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ; dhārtarāṣṭrāñ śvāpadā vyābhaṣanta gajendrāṇāṃ madagandhāṃś ca tīvrān; na sehire tava putrasya nāgāḥ
english: A clear wind was at the back of the Pāṇḍavas; at the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra the beasts of prey howled. The pungent rut-scent of the lordly elephants your son's elephants could not endure.

sanskrit: duryodhano hastinaṃ padmavarṇaṃ; suvarṇakakṣyaṃ jātibalaṃ prabhinnam samāsthito madhyagataḥ kurūṇāṃ; saṃstūyamāno bandibhir māgadhaiś ca
english: Duryodhana, mounted on a lotus-hued elephant, girt with golden girths, of noble strength and flowing with rut, stood in the midst of the Kurus, extolled by bards and panegyrists.

sanskrit: candraprabhaṃ śvetam asyātapatraṃ; sauvarṇī srag bhrājate cottamāṅge taṃ sarvataḥ śakuniḥ pārvatīyaiḥ; sārdhaṃ gāndhāraiḥ pāti gāndhārarājaḥ
english: His white parasol shone with the radiance of the moon, and a golden wreath gleamed upon his head; on every side Śakuni, king of Gāndhāra, guarded him with his hillmen and Gāndhāras.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo 'grataḥ sarvasainyasya vṛddhaḥ; śvetacchatraḥ śvetadhanuḥ saśaṅkhaḥ śvetoṣṇīṣaḥ pāṇḍureṇa dhvajena; śvetair aśvaiḥ śvetaśailaprakāśaḥ
english: At the head of the whole army stood the aged Bhīṣma, with white parasol, white bow, and conch, white-turbaned, with a pale banner and white horses, gleaming like a mountain of white.

sanskrit: tasya sainyaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca sarve; bāhlīkānām ekadeśaḥ śalaś ca ye cāmbaṣṭhāḥ kṣatriyā ye ca sindhau; tathā sauvīrāḥ pañcanadāś ca śūrāḥ
english: His army comprised all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, one portion of the Bāhlīkas and Śala, the Ambaṣṭha warriors and the Kṣatriyas dwelling by the Sindhu, and the valiant Sauvīras and men of the Five Rivers.

sanskrit: śoṇair hayai rukmaratho mahātmā; droṇo mahābāhur adīnasattvaḥ āste guruḥ prayaśāḥ sarvarājñāṃ; paścāc camūm indra ivābhirakṣan
english: With his blood-red horses and golden chariot, the great-souled, mighty-armed Droṇa of undaunted spirit—the teacher, renowned among all kings—stood guarding the host from the rear like Indra.

sanskrit: vārddhakṣatriḥ sarvasainyasya madhye; bhūriśravāḥ purumitro jayaś ca śālvā matsyāḥ kekayāś cāpi sarve; gajānīkair bhrātaro yotsyamānāḥ
english: In the midst of the whole army stood the son of Vṛddhakṣatra, with Bhūriśravas, Purumitra, and Jaya; and the Śālvas, Matsyas, and all the Kekaya brothers stood ready to fight with their elephant-divisions.

sanskrit: śāradvataś cottaradhūr mahātmā; maheṣvāso gautamaś citrayodhī śakaiḥ kirātair yavanaiḥ pahlavaiś ca; sārdhaṃ camūm uttarato 'bhipāti
english: The great-souled son of Śaradvat, the mighty archer of Gautama's line, skilled in varied modes of war, held the northern flank and guarded the host from the north with Śakas, Kirātas, Yavanas, and Pahlavas.

sanskrit: mahārathair andhakavṛṣṇibhojaiḥ; saurāṣṭrakair nairṛtair āttaśastraiḥ bṛhadbalaḥ kṛtavarmābhigupto; balaṃ tvadīyaṃ dakṣiṇato 'bhipāti
english: With the great chariot-warriors of the Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis, and Bhojas, with the Saurāṣṭrakas and Nairṛtas, weapons in hand, Kṛtavarman of mighty strength, well-guarded, protected your force from the south.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakānām ayutaṃ rathānāṃ; mṛtyur jayo vārjunasyeti sṛṣṭāḥ yenārjunas tena rājan kṛtāstrāḥ; prayātā vai te trigartāś ca śūrāḥ
english: A myriad chariots of the saṃśaptakas, sworn either to die or to conquer Arjuna, were sent forth; and wherever Arjuna was, there, O king, those weapon-skilled and valiant Trigartas advanced.

sanskrit: sāgraṃ śatasahasraṃ tu nāgānāṃ tava bhārata nāge nāge rathaśataṃ śataṃ cāśvā rathe rathe
english: A hundred thousand elephants and more were yours, O Bhārata; for every elephant a hundred chariots, and for every chariot a hundred horses,

sanskrit: aśve 'śve daśa dhānuṣkā dhānuṣke daśa carmiṇaḥ evaṃ vyūḍhāny anīkāni bhīṣmeṇa tava bhārata
english: for every horse ten bowmen, and for every bowman ten shield-bearers: thus were the divisions arrayed by Bhīṣma for you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: avyūhan mānuṣaṃ vyūhaṃ daivaṃ gāndharvam āsuram divase divase prāpte bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'graṇīḥ
english: Day after day as it came, Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu and foremost of leaders, set up the array—now human, now divine, now gandharva, now demonic.

sanskrit: mahārathaughavipulaḥ samudra iva parvaṇi bhīṣmeṇa dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ vyūhaḥ pratyaṅmukho yudhi
english: Vast with its flood of great chariot-warriors, like the sea at the turn of the moon, the array of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, set up by Bhīṣma, faced westward in the battle.

sanskrit: anantarūpā dhvajinī tvadīyā; narendra bhīmā na tu pāṇḍavānām tāṃ tv eva manye bṛhatīṃ duṣpradhṛṣyāṃ; yasyā netārau keśavaś cārjunaś ca
english: Boundless in form was your banner-host, O lord of men, and fearsome—yet not so the Pāṇḍavas'. Still, theirs I deem the mighty and unassailable one, whose leaders are Keśava and Arjuna.
